g.text: Thursday 6 August, 14:00. Headquarters approve of memory. They have sent a list of libraries that
provide it, and Strand's covering note says any of them would spare the unit the work of keeping its
own. His team could clean up the old store while they moved it.
Varma writes one word in the margin beside that line. No.
She reads the list as she read the last three. "Which of these run in this building?"
That is the first test and it is not a small one. A memory library that calls a hosted model to decide
what to remember has sent the evidence out of the door.
"And the second test," Okafor says. "Which of them can tell me who wrote an entry."

. What each one decided for you
The same four tasks, arm by arm
On the lab's store the eighth entry was held at the gate, recall returned 1 entries, and after
retraction its text and all 2 events on it are still there, with eow-fin-07 and svc-lantern-sync against
it. The memory tool's 10 commands, carried out on the same store, held the Pellmar file and kept its
text, marked, after delete; the commands carry no author, so the log names LANTERN. Given the tool,
LANTERN wrote 1 file(s), 0 kept. Mem0: stored 5 memories from two lines, 0 word for word, and with
telemetry left on tried 5 connections off the machine, every one refused. Graphiti, Letta and Zep were
read about, not run. None of them can say who wrote an entry unless it is told; the recommendation is
the lab's own store, with the memory tool's commands as the way a hosted model reaches it.
